board: Mid War: corpus positions seed 4001 T7 AR1 (US seat) and seed 4000 T7 AR1 (USSR seat), from tests/corpus/positions.json.gz
unit: Seat-own Ops: US Ops on the US position, USSR Ops on the USSR position, positive is good for the seat that holds the card. (Claude's call, offered to the expert.)

Junta.note: Generally 4: as the US you still get the coup; as the USSR you can swing two battlegrounds by breaking one, couping the other, and dumping 4 Ops on AR1.

Bear_Trap.note: ~3.5 base, but very hand dependent and it moves up with Red Scare/Purge. In the right hand it beats Voice of America (6+), so treat 3.5 as the floor, not the ceiling.

Nuclear_Subs.note: How many extra battleground Ops you get out of couping Africa's 1-stability countries: 3-4. The USSR can force defence, but that costs them an Op each.

ABM_Treaty.note: About right at the bot's 5.0; there are a lot of weird tricks with ABM.

Brush_War.note: Bot about right. Not about 1-stability targets: it hits every 2-stability target, an isolated country or one with a single adjacent support.

Grain_Sales_to_Soviets.note: Expert: basically impossible to play without Nuclear Subs as the USSR; always evented as the US, because you can always return the card. Number still to come.

The_Voice_Of_America.note: 6+ Ops for the US, the equivalent of De-Stalinization. Bot says 5.7, close.

Brezhnev_Doctrine.note: Same logic as Containment, and already priced that way: both are in OPS_MODIFIER_EVENTS and valued as the marginal Ops over the cards the beneficiary will still play this turn.

We_Will_Bury_You.note: Revised up from 2.75: more powerful than it looks because of the DEFCON degrade. Number to confirm.

Quagmire.note: As Bear Trap: ~3.5 base, hand dependent, moves up with Red Scare/Purge.

ABM_Treaty.note: Bot's value accepted (see the US row).

Allende.note: Conditional: 2 if Chile is uncontrolled or US-controlled, ~4 with Chile and Argentina empty, 0.5 if the USSR already controls Chile. The fixture position decides which applies; 2 recorded as the general case.

Cultural_Revolution.note: About 1 when it does not move the China card; the China card is easily 2.5 Ops in the Mid War, so 3.5 when it does.

Missile_Envy.note: A hand event, but very, very good.

OPEC.note: Depends on the VP it scores. Rule of thumb: 1 VP = 2 Ops in the Early War, 1 Op in the Mid War, 0.5 Op in the Late War (not sure).

Brezhnev_Doctrine.note: See the US row: already priced like Containment.

_vp_scale_note: Expert rule: 1 Op = 2 VP in the Early War (a VP is 0.5 Op), 1 Op = 1 VP in the Mid War, 2 Ops = 1 VP in the Late War. Encoded as StrategicWeights.vp_early/vp_mid/vp_late.

unpriceable._note: Events the sandbox cannot price: firing them on eight boards (opening, T5, T7, T9, both seats) moves no influence and no VP, so they value 0. Grouped by why. Rank or price these in Ops (seat-own) and the flag-event parameters get fitted to them. Some are 0 only because their eligibility was never met on those boards (Wargames and Cuban Missile Crisis need DEFCON 2; Solidarity needs John Paul II; Ortega needs a Nicaragua coup; Our Man in Tehran needs Iran).
